headline: Ancient and phased human genomes test selection and imputation inference methods
label: Comparative Evolutionary Genomics
summary: Ancient-DNA and haplotype-resolved assemblies now allow direct benchmarking of local ancestry, imputation, and selection inference methods.
synthesis: The common thread is the use of ancient and haplotype-resolved human genomes to evaluate evolutionary and population-genetic inference. A benchmark of eight local ancestry inference methods on 176 imputed Neolithic genomes recommends Gnomix or RFMix and tests selection signals at FADS1/2. Coalescent theory and simulations assess reference panel design for ancient DNA imputation, where a joint 1000 Genomes–ancient panel modestly improves rare-variant imputation. A study of genomic history and selection in Roman and early medieval Britain extends this framing to a regional historical setting. The HLA preprint is less directly inferential: it maps structural variation across 460 phased assemblies and links structural haplotypes to HLA expression differences. What is new is the pairing of explicit method benchmarking with archival material and haplotype-resolved structural comparison.
